takeaway: Quiet start to the week after Tropical Wave #47: Pacífico Norte looks mostly sunny this morning, then isolated afternoon showers on the peninsula — not a widespread storm day. Surf winds: light and mixed today, then cleaner night/morning offshore Mon night through Wednesday as Caribbean easterlies rebuild; Thursday looks softer again. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Mexico and farther west. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Mon–Wed)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s weather service says local heat and sea breezes run the show this week. Monday: few clouds in the morning over Pacífico Norte, then afternoon showers on the Nicoya Peninsula and eastern mountains; nights mostly quieter with only isolated coastal rain possible. Humidity should ease a bit from Monday night onward, but isolated Pacific showers continue. Hot inland (Nicoya around 33°C, Liberia near 35°C). Ensemble averages keep Nicoya daily rain mostly light to moderate — typical rainy-season cells, not a stuck rain machine. Mid-levels favor Caribbean easterlies across Nicaragua and Nicoya through midweek.
periods.implications: Best outdoor window is morning before isolated storms. For surf, do not count on all-day glass Monday; look for cleaner overnight and early sessions from tonight through Wednesday if the northerly/easterly turn holds.
periods.confidence: High that Monday is quieter than Saturday’s wave day and no nearby cyclone hits Costa Rica. Moderate on exact Nosara shower timing and how clean Tuesday–Wednesday mornings get.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Thu–Sun)
periods.pattern: Official longer outlook still leans drier than normal for Pacífico Norte into early October, with weekly Pacífico Norte totals roughly in a light-to-moderate rainy-season range and no extreme-rain event flagged. Ensemble averages show some moist days still possible — one wetter pulse shows up around the weekend in some means — but without a Costa Rica–centered rain machine. Near-surface marine winds look softer and more mixed Thursday; by Friday a west/northwest component returns on the Papagayo waters. Upper trades can lean Pacific-side later in the week.
periods.implications: Keep late-day plans flexible for quick storms. Surf-wind quality is better early in this stretch (still riding Mon–Wed trades) than Thursday–Friday if the Pacific-side flow verifies. Nicaragua all-day offshore earlier in the week is a good Nosara quality signal, but it does not mean Nosara stays glassy all day.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme and the midweek trade window; low–moderate for any weekend wetter spike or how firmly Thursday’s softer winds verify.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s longer-range outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal from late September into mid-October, with the dry signal strengthening after about October 12. No official extreme-rain event is flagged. Ensemble means still allow some moist days into early October, but the baseline is not a prolonged flood-season spell. Distant East Pacific activity remains focused near Mexico and farther west.
periods.implications: Treat any wet day as a short cell unless a new watch develops. Outdoor and surf planning can assume the quieter Pacífico Norte lean until guidance changes.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme; low for day-by-day detail past about a week.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: No focused window; residual leftover moisture Monday, then only a general chance of a wetter pulse later in the week or weekend if Pacific moisture reconnects
gyreWatch.supporting: Weekend Tropical Wave #47 left some leftover instability into Sunday–Monday. Broad moist Pacific flow remains nearby offshore. Some ensemble means show a wetter day around the weekend. Distant East Pacific storms keep the far-Pacific moisture field active near Mexico.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No closed gyre sits over Costa Rica or Nicaragua on the main ensemble averages. Official Monday Pacífico Norte forecast is only peninsula/mountain afternoon showers under local factors. Humidity is expected to ease from Monday night. Midweek Caribbean easterlies argue against a stuck onshore rain machine. The longer official outlook leans drier for northern Pacific into October, with no extreme event flagged for this week. Named East Pacific systems track along or well off Mexico, not toward Costa Rica.

surfWinds.regime: Light/mixed Monday → Caribbean easterlies / N–NW Mon night–Wed → softer/mixed Thu, Pacific-lean possible later week
surfWinds.detail: Papagayo waters: light variable under 5 kt today — that is not glassy all-day offshore. Tonight winds turn northwest to north around 10 kt, holding NW–N Tuesday and Wednesday — the classic offshore setup for west-facing Nosara. Thursday looks softer/more mixed (light variable at Papagayo, west–northwest elsewhere); Friday trends west–northwest again. Mid-level maps agree on Caribbean easterlies across Nicaragua and Nicoya through midweek (stronger over Nicaragua). That Nicaragua all-day offshore signal usually means good Nosara morning quality, but Nosara is not necessarily offshore all day. Do not read Papagayo light/variable as all-day glass.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Early morning Monday before the sea breeze. Cleaner overnight/morning glass Mon night through Wednesday if trades hold. Thursday less reliable. No clean all-day offshore Monday signal.
surfWinds.confidence: High on Monday daytime light/mixed and the NW–N rebuild tonight into Tuesday. Moderate on how firmly Wednesday holds and whether Thursday–Friday lean Pacific/onshore.

whatChanged: Wave #47’s direct influence is over; Monday’s official Pacífico Norte call is local-factor showers on the peninsula, not a wave day. Sunday’s storm notice (residual instability after the wave) is aging — no new Monday notice yet. Tropical Storm Rachel is the nearest East Pacific named system (south-southwest of Acapulco); Polo and Nolo remain well west — none threaten Costa Rica. Surf-wind improvement from tonight through midweek still looks on track. Prolonged-rain watch stays watch-only.
practical: Best outdoors: Monday morning before isolated afternoon storms; heat inland continues. For surf, prioritize early morning today; look for cleaner easterly/N–NW glass from tonight through Wednesday. Prolonged multi-day rain is not the baseline. Latest official storm notice: Sunday 27 Sep 9:40 a.m. (leftover instability after Wave #47).
